newsitem.title: USA: U.S corp debt mart quiet, players plot next move.
newsitem.headline: U.S corp debt mart quiet, players plot next move.

text.p: A quiet day is expected in the corporate debt new issue arena as players digest Friday's U.S. economic data and plot their strategies for the upcoming week, dealers said.
"It's going to be a real yawner...the market tone is good but there's no business scheduled for today," said one high-grade syndicate source. "If you have golf clubs, get them out," he added.
Earlier, the U.S. Labor Department reported a bigger-than-expected drop in the April unemployment rate to 4.9 percent. April payrolls increased by 142,000, Labor said.
Labor said the 4.9 percent U.S. unemployment rate was the lowest since 1973.

U.S. Treasuries struggled for direction immediately following the report's release, jumping higher in a knee-jerk reaction. The 30-year bond gained a half point only to quickly retreat back to opening levels.
Currently, the T-bond is quoted off 9/32 at 96-2/32 to yield 6.94 percent.
Dealers said with Treasury yields below 7.0 percent, the calendar could pick up steam in the week ahead.

In the high-grade primary sector, no new issues have priced; however, CSX Corp's successfully priced $2.5 billion multi-tranche debt offering, priced on Thursday, was seen at a tighter spread when freed to trade," players said.
"CSX's issues tightened across the board by about one to three basis pointse," one high-grade syndicate source said.

Salomon Brothers, the underwriter for the deal, upsized the offering to $2.5 billion, from $2.0 billion, and restructured the offering to include an additional 30-year issue, putable in 8-years, a 35-year tranche, and a 10-year tranche, putable in five years, sources said.
Other issues included a five-year, seven-year, 10-year and 30-year maturities, sources said.

Meanwhile, another large debt offering is in the works, players said. Norfolk Southern Corp is expected to issue between $3.0 and $4.0 billion in a multi-tranche debt offering via joint lead managers Merrill Lynch and JP Morgan Securities.
Also, Dominion Resources is slated to bring $800 million in Baa1/A-minus rated debt offering next week consisting of five and 10-year debt. Lehman Brothers is expected to underwrite the deal.
In addition, Briggs & Stratton Corp is expected to set $175 million in five and 10-year debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.

Turning to the high-yield sector, net cash inflows into U.S. high-yield mutual funds for the week ended April 30, increased to $760.2 million, setting a new all time high, according to AMG Data Services.

A total of $1.32 billion in new cash has poured into the high-yield market since the week ended April 16. The market experienced around $1.58 billion of net cash outflows in the prior four weeks, according to AMG Data.

In other news on Friday, Pride Petroleum Services issued $325 million in 10-year Ba3/BB-minus rated senior notes to yield 9.375 percent, sources said. The deal was increased from an initial size of $300 million, they said.
Colorado Prime Corp is expected to issue $100 million in 144A 10-yeare notes via JP Morgan Securities later today, sources said. Price talk is ssen in the 12 percent area.
Among other upcoming high-yield offerings expected next week are Comcast Cellular's $900 million 144A senior 10-year note offering via Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, sources said.
Also, Cityscape Financial Corp is expected to issue $300 million in senior notes due 2004 via CIBC.
French Fragrances Inc is also expected to tap the market with $100 million in senior notes due 2007 via DLJ Securities.
Other names include GST Telecom Inc's $230 million, Reliant Building Products' $70 million, and Western Star Holdings Ltd's $100 million, debt offerings, sources said.
